mutants.description: hiccup_timer is handed strike_level plus one, as if it had to anticipate strike_counter's increment on entry to S_HICCUP, so every cool-down is one doubling longer than the strike count calls for
mutants.reason: strike_counter has already incremented by the time the cool-down runs, so the first hiccup lasts base<<2 (20 ms by default) instead of base<<1 (10 ms), and at strike level 3 the 2-bit sum wraps to the base interval. The time En is held low in S_HICCUP before the retry into S_SS changes on every hiccup.

mutants.description: MISO is tri-stated outside the read-data phase, following the usual shared-bus SPI slave habit, instead of being driven low as a plain output
mutants.reason: At every time except spi_slave's S_READ phase (idle, command, address and write phases), MISO floats at Z instead of reading 0. That breaks the header's rule that MISO is a plain output with no tri-state anywhere in the design.

mutants.description: pwm_stats measures the synchronised modulator PWM only while the gate driver is enabled, though its block comment says it runs unconditionally because duty and period matter as much during a fault
mutants.reason: In S_OFF and S_HICCUP, or while a hard fault pulls En low, the modulator still toggles Osc_in, but pwm_stats sees a flat line. Its period counter saturates and DUTY_COUNT and PERIOD stop following the modulator, so SPI reads of those registers return stale or all-ones values.

mutants.description: The housekeeping changeover drive is held on for one extra clock after PGOOD drops, ORed with the registered pgood_LED copy as a glitch hold-off, so the hand-back is no longer immediate
mutants.reason: switch_supply still rises with PGOOD, but when PGOOD deasserts (the rail leaves its window, or the converter leaves S_RUN) switch_supply stays high one clock longer. At that moment it differs from PGOOD, against the header's rule that it carries the same value with no added delay.
